title: Honoka Hashimoto and Shunsuke Togami win WTT Star Contender Muscat as Japan take four titles
seo_title: WTT Star Contender Muscat 2026: Hashimoto and Togami win
description: Honoka Hashimoto beat Kaho Akae 4-2 for her second title in a week and Shunsuke Togami beat Park Ganghyeon 4-1 at WTT Star Contender Muscat 2026.
standfirst: The Japanese defender saved a game point in the sixth game of the women's final, Togami added the mixed doubles with Satsuki Odo, and no Chinese player reached a final.

body: Honoka Hashimoto won her second title in seven days at WTT Star Contender Muscat on Saturday, beating her Japanese team-mate Kaho Akae 4-2 in the final, and Shunsuke Togami took the men's title by beating South Korea's Park Ganghyeon 4-1 before adding the mixed doubles with Satsuki Odo. Japan won four of the five titles in Oman.

Hashimoto, the 28-year-old defender who won [WTT Contender Istanbul](/news/wtt-contender-istanbul-2026-finals-fang-bo-honoka-hashimoto-titles.html) last Sunday, has now won 10 matches in a row on the WTT tour. It is her first Star Contender singles title, after defeats in the finals in Bangkok in 2024 and Chennai in 2025. Togami's win is his third WTT singles title of the year, after the WTT Star Contender in Ljubljana in June and the WTT Contender in Almaty in September.
## Hashimoto saves a game point to win it

Akae won the first game 12-10 and led 2-1 after taking the third 11-4. Hashimoto, the second seed, levelled at 11-7 and went ahead at 11-6, then trailed 5-2 in the sixth and faced a game point at 10-9 before winning the last three points, according to Taiwan's United Daily News. The final lasted 58 minutes. Akae, 22 and ranked 36th, was playing her first WTT final above Feeder level.

Hashimoto had beaten Romania's Bernadette Szőcs, the fifth seed, 11-6, 11-4, 9-11, 11-4 in the semi-finals. Akae knocked out the top seed: she beat Odo 11-6, 13-11, 12-14, 11-9, her second win over a Japanese seed in two days after coming from two games down against Miyu Nagasaki in the quarter-finals.

Her five wins in Muscat came against players from five countries and included a 3-0 win over Taiwan's Cheng I-Ching in the quarter-finals. She now leads Akae 4-0 in their meetings at WTT events since 2021, in Eleven's records.
## Togami recovers from a game down

Park, 30 and the world No 44, won the first game of the men's final 11-6. Togami, the second seed and the world No 15, took the next three 11-6, 11-7, 11-5 and won the fifth 16-14 after 38 minutes. It was Park's first WTT final above Feeder level; he had beaten the 18-year-old qualifier Sun Yang, France's Flavien Coton and then his compatriot Oh Junsung, 11-7, 6-11, 11-6, 11-9, in the semi-finals.

Togami dropped two games in five singles matches all week. He beat Chen Yuanyu, China's last player in either singles draw, 11-6, 12-10, 11-3 in 22 minutes in the semi-finals, then played the mixed doubles final an hour later. He and Odo beat France's Esteban Dorr and Jia Nan Yuan 11-6, 11-5, 12-14, 11-3, giving Odo her second title in two days after the women's doubles with Sakura Yokoi on Friday.
## Japan's four titles and China's blank

South Korea's Lim Jonghoon and Oh Junsung won the men's doubles, the only title that did not go to Japan. No Chinese player reached a final. Chinese media counted Togami's win as the 12th WTT event in a row in which no Chinese man had won the singles title, a run they described as a warning about the depth of the national team behind its leading players.

Japan won the four titles without five of their best-known players, Tomokazu Harimoto, Miwa Harimoto, Hina Hayata, Sora Matsushima and the defender Hitomi Sato, none of whom entered, as the Chinese portal Sohu pointed out in its report. Sohu also wrote that chopping had long been seen as old-fashioned and passive, and that Hashimoto's two titles had shown how the style is changing.

Togami, Odo, Hashimoto and Hiroto Shinozuka travel to Chengdu for the [Mixed Team World Cup](/events/mixed-team-world-cup-2026.html), which starts on 29 November, in Japan's eight-player squad. Park, Oh, Lim and Kim Nayeong are in South Korea's. The ranking points from Muscat count in the world ranking published on Tuesday.

- Semi-final: Kaho Akae (JPN) bt Satsuki Odo (JPN) 11-6, 13-11, 12-14, 11-9

Men's singles:

- Semi-final: Park Ganghyeon (KOR) bt Oh Junsung (KOR) 11-7, 6-11, 11-6, 11-9

Doubles finals:
- Mixed: Shunsuke Togami and Satsuki Odo (JPN) bt Esteban Dorr and Jia Nan Yuan (FRA) 11-6, 11-5, 12-14, 11-3
- Women's (Friday): Satsuki Odo and Sakura Yokoi (JPN) bt Kim Nayeong and Joo Cheonhui (KOR) 11-7, 11-9, 11-6
- Men's (Friday): Lim Jonghoon and Oh Junsung (KOR) bt Manav Thakkar and Manush Shah (IND) 10-12, 11-2, 11-8, 11-8
